source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: English Genesis 32:1–32 is bound to Hebrew Gen 32:2–33. Hebrew Gen 32:1 is already bound to English Genesis 31:55 in the preceding ledger. Numbering realigns at Genesis 33.

key_decisions.decision: Preserve the property list and make the enslaved status of the gender-specific servants explicit; render favor-in-your-eyes naturally without promising Esau’s response.
Identify Abraham’s actual relationship to Jacob while retaining the ancestral prayer formula, the divine name, command, and promise.
Render Jacob’s smallness as unworthiness, preserve the paired covenant qualities, and clarify what became two camps without losing the staff-to-abundance contrast.
Keep the repeated brother/Esau identification, Jacob’s admitted fear, and the source’s concrete image of wholesale destruction.
Make the servants’ enslaved status visible, keep their entrusted task, and preserve the deliberate spacing of separate herds.
Retain Jacob’s strategy and uncertainty; keep one face expression in the text and disclose the source’s denser face wordplay in a note.
Preserve the timing, exact family counts, place name, and the women’s enslaved status rather than presenting them as employees.
Resolve the otherwise confusing pronouns from the narrative sequence while preserving the opponent’s failure, touch, injury, and ongoing struggle.
Preserve the new name, its struggle word association, both divine and human opponents, and the consequential claim of prevailing.
Preserve Jacob’s own identification, the Peniel/face association, and the surprising survival claim.
Retain the narrator’s later community perspective, bodily detail, dietary practice, and causal connection while avoiding a false anatomical precision.
